entries.description: "Oh, she's done very well for herself. Very well indeed." The smile didn't reach his eyes. It didn't even try.
"Hope's a fine thing. I had some once."
"This city used to mean something." Probably says this about everywhere they've ever lived.
"No no, don't mind me. Nobody ever does."
Perfectly polite. Perfectly pleasant. Has not forgiven a single person in this room.
"Well hello there! Don't your scales just shimmer in the sunlight? Care for a drink? or a song?" - said the bard to the ancient red dragon.
"Your eyes remind me of the moon at dusk. Tragic that I never had the patience for poetry."
"I never forget a face, especially one worth remembering." - said to the same stranger, three cities in a row.
"Shall we settle this like gentlemen?" - even with swords drawn, the enemy smiles.
"I do hope you'll forgive me," she said, leaving anyway.
"I have a plan," they announce, with the confidence of someone whose last plan burned down a mill.
"I've survived three wars, two famines, and a marriage. At this point death seems redundant."
"Ah yes, I remember my dignity. Good times." - said after picking themselves up from the gutter while covered in various "fluids".
Operates on a logic that almost makes sense. The almost is doing a lot of work.
"It got a little out of hand," regarding an incident that three separate bards have already written songs about.
Listens far more than they speak. When they do speak, you realise they've been three steps ahead the entire conversation.
Never lies. Simply chooses which truths to share, and when.
Has at least three versions of their own name depending on who's asking.
Plays games with very long endings. Most people don't realise they're playing.
Spotted the angle before you finished the sentence. Was already moving before you asked.
Answers questions with the minimum possible words. Not rude. Just tired.
Stopped making plans. Plans imply a future worth organising.
Smiles at the right moments. It's very convincing. It doesn't mean anything.
Has the eyes of someone who has seen too much and slept too little. In that order.
Not unhappy exactly. Just finished. Like a book someone forgot to pick back up.
"I don't want to say I'm the best. I just can't think of anyone better."
Asks how you are. Doesn't wait for the answer. Tells you how they are instead.
Cannot receive a compliment without immediately topping it with a better one about themselves.
Listens politely to your opinion. Files it immediately under irrelevant.
Dresses like they're expecting a portrait to be painted at any moment.
"I like you," they say. They mean: you are currently useful to me.
Owns a great deal of things. None of them were free. Some of them weren't for sale.
Genuinely believes that wanting something badly enough is a form of deserving it.
Never the first to reach for the bill. Never the last to reach for the share.
Tips poorly. Remembers every copper they were ever shortchanged. These are not contradictions to them.
"Do you ever think about why we do any of this?" Yes. Constantly. It hasn't helped.
Keeps a journal. Has kept many journals. Has burned most of them.
Notices things. Rarely mentions them. Thinks about them for weeks.
Often found staring at something unremarkable for an uncomfortably long time.
"I'm still figuring it out," regarding themselves, at an age where most people have stopped trying.
Makes strangers feel like old friends within minutes. This is not a trick. They simply like people.
"This is going to be great," they say, about everything, and somehow they're usually correct.
Laughs first and loudest at their own jokes. Somehow this makes them funnier, not less.
Will help you move, help you grieve, help you celebrate, and show up to all three with food.
"Could be worse!" It could. Somehow around them it rarely is.
"Ah, interesting — did you know that—" They have been saying this their entire life.
Brilliant in ways that don't always include remembering to eat, sleep, or notice the room is on fire.
"Simply put—" Nothing they say is ever simply put.
Has one particular subject they care about more than is entirely healthy. Will find a way to bring it up.
Spent thirty years learning everything there is to know. Spent the next ten unlearning most of it.
Something small and unexplained happens whenever they're surprised. They've stopped apologising for it.
Speaks about distant places and ancient events as though they were there recently. They may have been.
"Oh that," they say, about something that should not have just happened.
Finds coins, hunger, and weather mildly amusing concerns that apply mostly to other people.
Looks at you like they can see something slightly behind you. You turn around. Nothing is there.
Has a different past depending on who's asking. All versions are equally plausible.
Appears where needed. Leaves before questions form. Has never once been late.
Reacts to certain names, certain places, certain years — just barely. Just enough to notice.
"That's a good question," they say, and then simply don't answer it.
Smiles at things other people don't notice. Never explains what they found amusing.
Arrived early to check the exits. Knows exactly how many people are in the room. Has a plan.
Doesn't eat food they didn't see prepared. Considers this perfectly reasonable. It might be.
"Who sent you?" They're joking. Probably. The pause before the laugh is a little long.
Apologises for being nervous. Does not stop being nervous.
Would love to relax. Has simply never found a situation that warranted it.
Agrees with you warmly and completely. Later you'll realise they didn't actually agree with anything.
Remembers who was in the room for every important conversation they've ever had. Just in case.
"What I can tell you is—" Everything after this is true. Everything before it was the real message.
Has never once said what they meant on the first try. Considers this a professional courtesy.
Has seen enough to know how it all works. Has not yet decided what to do with that knowledge.
Processes catastrophe the way most people process mild inconvenience. Slowly, quietly, completely.
"Mm." This means many things. You'll learn to read it eventually.
Doesn't complain. Not out of pride. It simply hasn't occurred to them that it would help.
Offers no comfort. Offers presence. Most people find this is enough.
"It is what it is," they say, and somehow from them it doesn't sound like giving up.
Incorrect with impressive consistency. Never deterred. Never right.
Misses every subtext, implication, and social cue. Enjoys conversations enormously as a result.
Means well, tries hard, and arrives at the wrong conclusion via a route nobody could have predicted.
Their logic almost holds together. The almost is load-bearing.
Has survived entirely on luck, instinct, and the goodwill of smarter people. Shows no signs of stopping.
Smiles a lot. The smile doesn't reach the eyes. The eyes are doing something else entirely.
"It's not personal," they say, which is somehow worse than if it were.
Moves through crowds the way water moves around stone — always the path of least resistance, always aware of every obstacle.
Bored by peace. Not because they don't value it. Because they don't know what to do with themselves inside it.
Has hurt a lot of people. Keeps a rough count. Doesn't share it. Doesn't forget it.
The faith isn't something they have. It's something they are. The distinction matters to them enormously.
Genuinely cannot conceive that you might hear the truth and still choose to walk away from it.
Prays constantly — not performatively, not dutifully. Like breathing. Like they'd die without it.
"I have no fear of death," they say. You believe them. This is not reassuring.
Loved ones lost, comforts abandoned, doubts silenced. Calls it a fair trade. May still be deciding.
